anya: quick summary from today's kv-slot-drift run on raptor-30b
anya: ran KV-only quant profiles: fp8-kv (AWQ pipeline) vs int8-kv (generic gptq)
anya: config used:
```bash
./bench_kv.sh --model raptor-30b --ctx 128k --batch 1,4 --warm 2 --runs 50 --kv-quant {fp8,int8}
```
sam: numbers?
anya: table (avg tokens/sec / p50 / p95 / p99 / kv-mem):
- FP8-KV: 420 tps / 2.4ms / 3.1ms / 8.0ms / 6.8GB
- INT8-KV: 390 tps / 2.6ms / 3.5ms / 8.6ms / 5.1GB
anya: so INT8 wins on memory (-25%), but we see p99 shift +0.6ms absolute (~7.5%) on 1-batch cold-starts
liam: did you split warm vs cold? could be dequant penalty on miss path causing extra memcpy
anya: yes; cold path (no prefix cache) shows the worst delta. warm path p99 identical within noise
jordan: eviction counts? maybe INT8 increases cache churn because blocks smaller -> more frequent writes
anya: eviction delta small (+3% writes) — I think access pattern stayed same
sam: any repro of quality regressions? fp8->int8 could change fp accumulation
anya: ran perplexity eval on evalset: diff <0.2% for top-5 tokens. not significant
liam: suggestion: try hybrid -> store hot keys in fp8, colder keys int8. tradeoff mem vs latency
anya: agreed, going to schedule hybrid shadow on canary (run id: run-2695001)
ci-runner-bot: bench run completed: gs://bench-artifacts/2695001/summary.html
jordan: can you post the grafana link for p99 traces?
anya: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/kv/kv-slot-drift?orgId=1&panelId=4&from=now-1h
sam: thanks — next: test batch 8 and 32 to see aggregation impact
anya: noted, will run tomorrow and post short notes :thumbsup:
